title: Four records for disodium β-glycerophosphate pentahydrate; one mapped, three not
body:
The Edison sweep surfaced the same CAS (13408-09-8) on records that turn out to
be four spellings of one substance:

| identifier | preferred_term | status | ontology_id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cas:13408-09-8` | `Na2glycerophosphate•5H2O` | MAPPED | CHEBI:15978 |
| `UNMAPPED_0101` | `Na2Glycerophosphate•5H2O` | UNMAPPED | — |
| `UNMAPPED_0081` | `Na2Glycerophosphate.5H2O` | UNMAPPED | — |
| `UNMAPPED_0465` | `Na2 beta-glycerol PO4 x 5 H2O` | UNMAPPED | — |

The mapped record and `UNMAPPED_0101` differ **by the case of a single letter**
(`glycerophosphate` vs `Glycerophosphate`). `UNMAPPED_0081` differs from
`UNMAPPED_0101` only in `.` vs `•`.

The mapped record was grounded during this sweep, per MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3
— `cas:` identifier plus `skos:narrowMatch` to CHEBI:15978 plus the Rule B1
registry row. The three unmapped siblings did not move, so the same substance is
now both mapped and unmapped depending on which spelling a medium happens to use.

Also worth noting: `Beta-Glycerophosphate disodium salt hydrate` is separately
mapped as `cas:154804-51-0` -> CHEBI:17270, so there may be a fifth member with
an unspecified hydration state.

No gate catches this. `qc-duplicate-ids` compares identifiers, and these have
four distinct ones; `reconcile_sssom.py` sees no drift because unmapped records
are not expected to publish rows.

Two things to decide, and I don't think they should be decided together:

1. **Are these duplicates?** Almost certainly yes for the three `5H2O` spellings.
   `Na2 beta-glycerol PO4 x 5 H2O` reads the same but is a looser paraphrase, so
   it deserves a separate look.
2. **Should they be merged onto `cas:13408-09-8`, or should the mapped record be
   reconsidered?** The reports hedge on the CAS itself: 13408-09-8 is linked to
   β-glycerophosphate but the retrieved sources "do not explicitly confirm that
   this CAS is the exact disodium pentahydrate form rather than a less-specific
   parent/supplier entry", and a second report says the evidence "does not fully
   establish that CAS 13408-09-8 always denotes a rigorously fixed 5-hydrate
   material". Merging three records onto that identifier propagates a hedge to
   four records instead of one.

Nothing applied. CAS enrichment on the two candidates was deliberately withheld
pending this, and the refusals are recorded in
`scripts/apply_edison_cas_enrichment.py`.

The case-only difference is the same drift as #293 and #236, appearing here as
duplicate records rather than as subject/file mismatch.
